title: Cash, Card & Payment Security
blurb: How to protect guests and the venue from card fraud, tampered card machines and cash problems.
siteNotes: Who authorises refunds, voids and manual key-entry on each shift.
Who to report suspected fraud or counterfeit notes to.
legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer refers to "PCI" standards. PCI DSS is the card industry's data security standard, set by the card schemes rather than by law; the slides only say card payments come with rules. Please confirm the venue's card provider requirements.
Storing card data is also a data protection matter (UK GDPR); not quoted on slides.

cards.title: Cash, Card & Payment Security
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- handle card details the safe way
- spot a tampered card machine
- get refunds authorised and report fraud

cards.title: Protecting guests and the venue
cards.body:
Handling payments carefully protects our guests from fraud and protects us from losses and card-data theft.

Card payments come with rules, the "PCI" standards, but most of it is common sense: treat card details like the sensitive information they are.

cards.title: What fraudsters want
cards.body:
Never write down or store a guest's full card number, and never take a photo of a card or email card details.

Handle a guest's card as little as possible, ideally letting them tap or insert it themselves. Refer anything odd about a card or the person using it to a manager.

left.title: Do
items: Let guests tap or insert their own card
Handle cards as little as possible
Refer anything odd to a manager

right.title: Do not
items: Write down a full card number

cards.title: Look after the machines
cards.body: Check card machines for signs of tampering or an extra device attached, known as a "skimmer". Report anything that looks wrong.

items.title: Check
items.text: Look for tampering or an extra device

items.title: Spot
items.text: A skimmer attached to the reader

items.title: Report
items.text: Tell a manager if it looks wrong

cards.title: Refunds, voids and key-entry
cards.body:
Refunds, voids and manual key-entry should be authorised by a supervisor or manager.

That protects you as well as the business.

items.title: Supervisor or manager
items.text: Authorises the refund, void or key-entry

cards.title: Cash, counted discreetly
cards.body:
Count and handle cash discreetly and out of guests' sight, and follow the cash-handling procedure.

Report any suspected fraud, counterfeit notes or discrepancies straight away. A little care at the payment stage stops a lot of problems later.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never write down or store a full card number, or photograph or email a card.
- Handle a guest's card as little as possible.
- Check card machines for tampering or an extra device.
- Refunds, voids and manual key-entry need a supervisor or manager.
- Report suspected fraud, counterfeit notes or discrepancies straight away.

cards.q: You should never write down or store a guest's full card number.
cards.why: Never write down or store a full card number; that is exactly what fraudsters want.

cards.q: Taking a photo of a guest's card is…
cards.why: Never take a photo of a card. Fraudsters want exactly that kind of record.

cards.q: What should you check card machines for?
options: Tampering or an extra device attached
Scratches on the casing or screen
Paper receipts left in the tray
cards.why: Check card machines for signs of tampering or an extra device attached, a "skimmer".

cards.q: Refunds and voids should be authorised by a supervisor or manager.
cards.why: Refunds, voids and manual key-entry should be authorised by a supervisor or manager, which protects you too.

cards.q: You should handle a customer's card…
options: Whenever it is quicker for you
Only when they are not looking
cards.why: Handle a guest's card as little as possible, ideally letting them tap or insert it themselves.

cards.q: Emailing card details is a safe way to record a payment.
cards.why: Never email card details. That is exactly what fraudsters want.

cards.q: What should you do if you suspect payment fraud or a counterfeit note?
options: Keep quiet until the end of shift
Report it straight away to a manager
Wait for it to happen again
cards.why: Report any suspected fraud, counterfeit notes or discrepancies straight away.

cards.q: Cash should be counted and handled discreetly, out of guests' sight.
cards.why: Count and handle cash discreetly and out of guests' sight.

cards.q: A device secretly attached to a card reader to steal data is called a…
cards.why: An extra device attached to a card machine is a "skimmer". Check machines for tampering and report anything wrong.

cards.q: Payment security protects both guests and the business.
cards.why: Careful handling protects guests from fraud and protects us from losses and card-data theft.
